title: 7-day moving average
summary: Smooth daily sign-ups with a trailing 7-day window, and only report full windows.
prompt: The growth dashboard plots daily sign-ups and their **7-day moving average**: the average of the day itself
Return `day`, `signups` and `avg_7d`, ordered by `day`. `avg_7d` is rounded to 2 decimals with `ROUND(..., 2)`,
and is `NULL` for the first days, until a full 7 days of data exist (a 3-day average labelled "7-day" misleads).
Every day has a row; there are no gaps.
setup: CREATE TABLE daily_signups (day TEXT PRIMARY KEY, signups INTEGER NOT NULL);
solution: CASE WHEN COUNT(*) OVER w = 7 THEN ROUND(AVG(signups) OVER w, 2) END AS avg_7d
WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
wrong: CASE WHEN ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY day) >= 7 THEN ROUND(AVG(signups) OVER (ORDER BY day), 2) END AS avg_7d
ROUND(AVG(signups) OVER (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS avg_7d
CASE WHEN COUNT(*) OVER w >= 7 THEN ROUND(AVG(signups) OVER w, 2) END AS avg_7d
WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
hints: `AVG(signups) OVER (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)` is a 7-row trailing window.
Without a frame, `OVER (ORDER BY day)` averages everything from the first day: a running average, not a moving one.
`COUNT(*)` over the same window tells you whether it is full; a named `WINDOW w AS (...)` saves writing it twice.
